claim_one_line: THE SECOND DEBT REGISTER MEETS THE FIRST, AND THE GATED ONE CANNOT SEE TWO-THIRDS OF THE CORPUS. THE OMISSION: docs/consolidation/DEBT_LEDGER.md, this refresh's own deliverable, was built and published through three versions without ever naming docs/REPRESENTATION_TRIAGE.md -- the repository's own register of unrepresented arcs (L143/B976), swept by scripts/checks/representation_sweep.py and enforced by a FAILING gate whose rule reads 'an untriaged unrepresented arc is the defect'. The two rules differ and each is right for its own question: the triage takes PROVED or NEGATIVE, filters on claim_one_line >= 500 characters, and reads 9 synthesis surfaces including working registers, asking 'is this represented anywhere a reader looks'; the ledger takes PROVED, applies no substantiality filter, and reads 5 curated consolidations, asking 'is this DISTILLED'. Counts: 234 against 10 live (17 rows, 13 PENDING), overlapping in 6 arcs. Neither is withdrawn; publishing one without the other is the defect, the same shape B1030 filed against THE_CLAIM vs B1000 with the unreferenced register this time being mine. B976, whose lead created the triage, sits in the ledger's rows and NOT in the triage, correctly -- it is cited on THE_SM_VERDICT and SM_SPECIFICATION_LEDGER, sweep surfaces rather than curated ones; both registers behaved as designed and only the cross-reference was missing. THE LARGER FINDING, and it is about a live gate: THE SUBSTANTIALITY BAR IS A STEP IN TIME, NOT A MEASURE OF SUBSTANCE. Median claim_one_line length runs 145-162 characters through B799 and then 733, 2571, 3084 in B800-899, B900-999, B1000+ -- the field changed from a one-line summary to an abstract around B800 -- so ZERO OF THE 731 ARCS BANKED BEFORE B800 CAN EVER CLEAR THE 500-CHARACTER BAR, and the gate that exists to catch 'a row that was never written' is structurally blind to two-thirds of the corpus. THIS IS NOT A MISCALIBRATION: the register was calibrated on the eleven lost cascade arcs B860-B873 (B862 excluded because another seat had cited it) and it does catch 11 of 11 -- a post-convention block. The bar is right for the job it was built for; what is missing is a stated era scope, the rule as written saying 'every SUBSTANTIAL banked arc'. THREE MEASUREMENTS THAT CHANGE WHAT SHOULD BE DONE ABOUT IT: (i) THE MARGIN ON ITS OWN CALIBRATION BLOCK IS TWO CHARACTERS -- B862, same block, the arc that DERIVES THE GLOBAL Z6 FORM, carries a claim line of 498 and is outside the calibration set only because a different seat cited it an hour earlier; had it not, '11 of 11' would have been 11 of 12 and the miss would have been the block's most consequential member. (ii) THE OBVIOUS REPAIR FAILS AND WAS TESTED BEFORE BEING OFFERED -- a band-relative threshold (>= 2x band median) recovers 1 of 12 of the calibration block, so trading a known blind spot for an unknown one is worse than naming the known one; registered as L158 rather than proposed as a fix. (iii) THE MEASURE THE REGISTER REJECTED IS THE ERA-STABLE ONE -- FINDINGS.md size holds a median of 2.0-5.5 KB in every band with no step, and its rejection was correct WITHIN the late era (B864's FINDINGS is 3.7 KB, short and dense, exactly the case that motivated the choice) but does not generalise; both decisions were locally right and the composition of them is the gap. CONSEQUENCE, AND THIS ARC REVERSES ITS OWN PLAN: the intended repair was to stratify the ledger's rows by that bar, 19 above and 215 below. REFUSED. Every one of the 19 is >= B870, so applying the bar would silently discard the entire pre-B800 corpus and import the blindness just measured; the rows stand unstratified. A SECOND, SMALLER CORRECTION: B1024 and B1026, both from this pass, cite 'docs/ERROR_LEDGER.md' as naming E1 the programme's most recurrent error class. ERROR_LEDGER.md never uses the phrase and registers E1 with 3 known instances, fewer than E4's or E12's; the claim is real and binding but lives in GOVERNANCE.md section 13 and WORKING_RULES.md. A MISATTRIBUTION, NOT A FALSE CLAIM -- stated at that size deliberately, because the first read of the evidence looked like a false claim and the spread-check corrected it; all three loci repointed in place, recorded as a retraction row because a citation to a document that does not contain the statement is exactly the corpus's E11 (overextended record). ON THE COUNT, WHICH MOVED 245 -> 251 -> 234: the measurement is moving by construction, every consolidation row added retiring a debt row, and this pass added eleven arcs' worth; the lock bounds the share rather than pinning the integer so ordinary consolidation work does not break it. One of those movements was not consolidation -- the 251 was computed against a working tree that had been rewound to an earlier commit, and the restored tree gives 234; THE STRUCTURAL FINDINGS WERE UNAFFECTED (0 of 731, the step function, the lowest above-bar row at B870), which is what a structural finding should do under a change of substrate, but the counts were wrong and were recomputed BEFORE publication rather than after. 24 mechanical checks importing the gate's own sweeper module rather than reimplementing it; 6 new locks appended to tests/test_consolidation_coverage.py; no mathematics asserted or disturbed; Gate 5 untouched; zero anchors; nothing to CLAIMS.md. Self-correction, one hazard now at five instances across four arcs: a consolidation arc that both MEASURES a gap and FILLS it invalidates its own metric unless the measurement is scoped by AUTHORSHIP -- here the register's new scope-limit note is what puts era language into the register, so the check for its absence had to exclude this arc's own block. THE_LADDER's X31 row named this first: 'Registering a gap creates hits for the gap, so the coverage count self-inflates.'
